verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents per-provider integration pages for cloud (AWS, via an AssumeRole role you can delete), identity (Google Workspace user accounts and Gmail settings), and code hosting (GitHub configuration, user access and Dependabot). The GitHub page notes it does not require access to repository contents, which points toward limited scopes. MDM appears only as Oneleet's own first-party MDM rather than a connector to an existing MDM, and HR and ticketing integrations are not evidenced. missing for 10: HR integrations, ticketing integrations, connectors to third-party MDM, an explicit read-only scope or permissions listing per integration, a browsable catalog overview, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can connect my real stack — cloud providers, identity, HR, code hosting, MDM, ticketing — through a documented integrations catalog with read-only scopes

citations.quote: Oneleet currently monitors the following AWS resources: Accounts, RDS instances, Application and Classic load balancers, IAM users
Oneleet uses the AWS AssumeRole API to work with AWS resources — if you'd like to remove Oneleet's access to your workspace, simply delete the created role
You can use it to monitor your GitHub configuration, user access, and Dependabot vulnerabilities. It does not require access to repository contents.
Oneleet currently monitors the following on Google Workspace: User accounts, GMail settings
